svg.title: LOCAL DELIVERY (GOPUFF): sketchnote
svg.text: It looks like an ordering system, but most of the load is people checking
Browsing availability is far more frequent than
ordering, so cache it and serve it from replicas.
Find nearby warehouses with an in-memory list
and a cheap distance filter before calling any
decrements for every item in one transaction.
Check availability of items deliverable to a location
Order multiple items; never sell stock you don't have
The DC list (10k rows) fits in memory.
Naive: call a travel-time API for every DC. 10k calls per page
Keep the small DC list in memory, prefilter by
straight-line distance, then ask travel time for
Browse reads come from a short-TTL cache and
read replicas. Slightly stale is fine here (AP).
Ordering hits the primary: one transaction with
UPDATE … SET qty = qty − n WHERE qty ≥ n
A conditional decrement per item inside one transaction; row locks serialize concurrent buyers.
Different consistency per path: browse is cached and eventually consistent; checkout reads
Partition inventory by region; an order only touches nearby DCs, so there are no cross-shard
Row contention on one inventory row: queue orders per item, or split stock into sub-buckets.
Redis as the inventory source of truth, with no
Adding parts before a number shows they are needed.
